fact: Chad has invested an estimated XAF 15 billion in recent years to build and strengthen its national biometric registry, which the government intends to make the single source of truth for identification, with ministries still being connected (Biometric Update citing Africa 24 TV and ANATS).
source_slug: 2026-03-16 Chad uses national biometric registry to boost govt systems interoperability

fact: SIGPTS, with technology from Idemia, enrolled Chadians in the National Biometric Population Register and issued National Identification Numbers (NNIs).
The system launched in 2020 able to deduplicate biometrics against a database of 15 million people within 10 seconds, per ChadInfos.

The ANATS site states that the SIGPTS, after enrolment and deduplication, assigns every individual, including refugees and resident or transiting foreigners, a unique randomly generated NNI, with 29 enrolment centres listed.
ANATS circular of 26 September 2025 says school leavers are enrolling to obtain their NNI, which the agency's centres issue.
The Chadian Presidency says ANATS agents will be posted permanently in embassies to deliver national identity cards and passports (announced by the President on 2025-09-10).
SIGPTS assigns a unique National Identification Number to registered individuals after enrolment and deduplication, per We are Tech.

Tchadinfos reports the national secure-titles agency ANATS said each beneficiary would receive a secure document tied to the Numero national d'identification (NNI), in an operation launched 27 July 2026.
